what_it_does_not_supply: the widths of lots 38-40 in feet: the lot sizes of the Assessor's Division block are not stated
the date the stable became a garage, the date the roof tiles were tarred, or any other change between 1887 and 1946 that it does not list
measurements: the data pages describe; the drawings (habs_glessner_house_il_1015_drawings) measure
what_it_supplies: the exterior construction as surveyed in 1963: foundations of Joliet limestone ending at the ground line; brick walls faced with alternately six- and eight-inch sheets of granite with deeper returns at openings; courtyard walls of light pink brick with Joliet limestone lintels and sills; steeply pitched gabled roofs covered with tar-covered terracotta tiles six inches wide, five inches exposed; copper sheathing on the roof of the entrance-hall bow
the original east carriage (porte-cochere) door as seen in a 1945 photograph: two heavily panelled leaves with heavy iron straps and latches
the list of 1946 alterations, which is the phase filter every 1963 dimension has to pass for 1904
the legal description and the March 1885 purchase of lots 39, 40 and the north 17 ft of lot 38
